name: Indian Potato-Cauliflower Curry (Aloo Gobi) with Cucumber Raita & Naan
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut off leaves from the cauliflower, separate into small florets, and cut the thick stems into smaller pieces. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Preheat a large pot over medium heat.
While the pot heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ginger, garlic, onion, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice potatoes; medium dice tomatoes. Add both to the bowl with the cauliflower.
Add spices to the pot and continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add cauliflower, potato, tomato, and broth to the pot; stir to combine and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to a simmer and cover; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, 15-18 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
While the curry cooks, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in the reserved bowl (reserving the rest for the curry).
Trim and grate cucumber into the bowl with the cilantro; add yogurt, water, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine the raita and set aside.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.

Divide naan between two baking sheet pans. Working in batches, place in the oven and broil, flipping once, until golden brown and toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven, spread with oil, and cut into quarters.
When the curry is done, stir in reserved cilantro and remove from the heat.
Divide curry between bowls; serve with raita and naan on the side. Enjoy!
author: Mealime
